transcript:
Header: 2026-06-11 16:00 PT | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Rossi (Redwood CSM); Carlos Ruiz (CTO, Cobalt), Jared Liao (Head of ML), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Mei Tan (SRE), Sara Bloom (Product)

Auto-summary: QBR focusing on platform economics and stability. High-level ask: reduce per-token cost by 12-18% without degrading p99 latency; investigate recurring 3-4x tail events during promo windows.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Carlos (Cobalt): Carlos here. Jared here. Priya here. Mei, Sara as well.
[00:00:12] Maya: Great. we're going to run through last quarter's usage, a cost deep dive, then reliability incidents and finally roadmap options — dedicated vs hosted and caching.

[00:02:10] Liam (Redwood SE): I'll jump into the usage trends — we pulled daily token burn for Q2. Overall steady growth ~18% month-over-month, but notable spike days around may 9 and june 3 during marketing promos. Those days drove 40% of new user churn in costs, basically a lot of short-lived high-concurrency traffic.
[00:02:45] Jared (Cobalt): yeah that matches our promo logs. we have a lot of concurrent cart completions that call the generative API ~300 RPS at peak.
[00:03:05] Priya (Cobalt): curious, are those requests mostly chat or single-shot generate?
[00:03:12] Liam: Mostly single-shot generation with a modest context (avg 350 tokens). a small subset are multi-turn chat that keep KV cache alive.

[00:05:00] Mei (Cobalt): On the reliability side we've seen these "tail" events where p99 jumps from 210ms to >900ms for 10-12 minutes during peak. We filed incident INC-447 twice.
[00:05:20] Liam: We traced that to a combination of cache invalidations and bursty batch sizes; when load crosses a batching boundary the runtime does a re-slice and you see higher latencies for a short window. Also a few requests fell back to a larger model variant due to routing thresholds.
[00:05:50] Sara (Cobalt): That fallback bit surprised us — didn't think fallback was kicking in.
[00:06:02] Maya: Right — routing policy currently is cost-first with a soft latency guard. We can flip to latency-first for specific routes (cart completions) as a pain-free change. We'll show the config.

[00:08:30] Carlos: Cost is our big pain. Our CFO asked why Q2 spend was up 27% vs plan. We need a breakdown per feature.
[00:08:42] Ava (CSM): We have a preliminary per-route breakdown, but we'll send a more granular one. Maya, can you comment on quantization and batching improvements?
[00:08:55] Maya: Sure — we can enable int8 quantization on the non-realtime routes and suggest conservative batching for the high-throughput endpoints. That typically saves ~15% token cost on encoder passes and up to 20% server-side compute costs, but there's tradeoffs for cold-start latency.
[00:09:30] Jared: Do we risk hallucinations or quality drops? We can't compromise output quality for cart completions.
[00:09:38] Liam: For single-turn cart completions quantization is safe; we validated on your prompt set with our eval harness (we used 2000 samples) — negligible quality delta. We should run a customer-specific eval to be sure.

[00:11:45] Priya: On dedicated vs hosted — if we go Dedicated, what is the minimum commit and timeline?
[00:11:52] Maya: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 60-90 days; minimum commit varies but we can propose a 3-month pilot with burst capacity enabled and flexible cap. We'll include pricing options in the cost sheet.
[00:12:20] Carlos: Would Dedicated reduce tail latency?
[00:12:25] Liam: Yes, Dedicated eliminates noisy neighbor effects and gives you reserved batch capacity; p99 and p999 stabilize a lot. But some tail behavior comes from batching thresholds and network jitter; those need runtime tuning too.

[00:14:30] Mei: about security — our compliance team requested SOC2 summary, audit logs, and KMS integration details.
[00:14:38] Ava: We have the SOC2 package and KMS docs; we'll share links after the call.
[00:14:45] Carlos: Will Dedicated expose more audit logs?
[00:14:49] Maya: Dedicated + Private control plane gives you richer audit trails and more retention options. We'll include retention tiers in the doc.

[00:16:55] Liam: Back to reliability — here's an action plan: 1) run a tail-latency profiling run during a scheduled spike, we capture batch-size distributions, 2) create a per-route latency-first policy for cart completions, 3) enable prefix/KV caching for multi-turn flows.
[00:17:20] Mei: We'll schedule a 2-hr bench window on june 22 when we expect a small promo.

[00:19:05] Sara: On roadmap alignment — we want features prioritized: 1) per-route latency SLOs, 2) cost-allocation dashboard by customer feature, 3) ability to pin model version for a route in production.
[00:19:25] Maya: All doable; per-route SLOs are in the roadmap for Q3 and pinning model versions already supported on Dedicated. We'll map priorities to your needs.

[00:21:50] Carlos: Can you also show a retrospective of past incidents and whether any were platform-side?
[00:21:58] Ava: We traced two incidents: one was a platform routing threshold misfire (we issued a bugfix in april), the other was customer traffic pattern leading to inefficient batching. We'll attach the postmortems.

[00:25:00] Jared: on the cost sheet, will you include per-token vs per-request splits? We need to see where tokens are coming from (system prompts, traces, user messages).
[00:25:12] Maya: Yes, we'll provide per-token categorization and suggested prompt truncation strategies for system messages.

[00:28:30] Liam: Quick note — enabling KV cache for multi-turn flows should reduce redundant prefix tokens and lower costs by ~10-12% for your conversational features.
[00:28:45] Priya: That seems promising. any risk to cold-start times?
[00:28:50] Liam: Cold-starts slightly higher, but with sticky sessions and warmers we can mitigate.

[00:32:00] Mei: A question on data residency — some EU customers require logs to remain in eu-west-1. Is that supported on Hosted or do we need Private?
[00:32:10] Maya: Hosted supports region pinning for data residency for many artifacts, but for full control Private deployment (VPC) is preferred. We'll call out the differences in the doc.

[00:36:15] Carlos: Let's recap next steps.
[00:36:20] Maya: We'll 1) send detailed cost breakdown and assumptions (Maya) by june 18, 2) schedule the 2-hr latency benchmark during a promo window (Liam) by june 25, 3) share SOC2 and KMS integration docs (Ava) by june 15, 4) propose Dedicated pilot options and pricing (Maya) by june 18.
[00:36:45] Carlos: Sounds good. Also please include a simple ROI calc showing when Dedicated pays back given our spike patterns.
[00:36:53] Maya: Will do.

[00:40:00] Sara: minor note — we saw a few odd transcriptions in the incident docs, can you attach raw traces?
[00:40:07] Liam: yes we'll include raw traces and a short explanation for each.

[00:44:10] Jared: quick ops ask — can we get an alert when cost/day > 2x baseline?
[00:44:17] Ava: We can configure threshold alerts and a cost anomaly cadence.

[00:48:00] Priya: any blockers from Redwood side for the pilot?
[00:48:07] Maya: none that I can see; just agreement on pilot duration and committed throughput.

[00:53:00] Carlos: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the bench and cost doc.
[00:53:08] Maya: thanks all.

End of transcript.
